A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain complete main text and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, proofs, figures, tables, and implementation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hamiltonian-cycle verification, Persona paraphrasing, and general-chat/math experiments, including additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in Figures 2–10, Tables 1–10, and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The EX-RM and IM-RM parameterizations, training objectives, and experimental variants are unchanged. The EX-GRM formulation and loss in Appendix A are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Hamiltonian-cycle, Persona, UltraFeedback, RewardMATH, and RewardBench math/code coverage, including paraphrased responses and French/Spanish translations.

E2.justification: The same EX-RM, IM-RM, and EX-GRM comparisons are reported. Figure 7 retains the all-representations EX-RM and reference-free IM-RM variants. The new DPO-versus-RLHF discussion adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The data splits, filtering, model configurations, training budgets, accuracy metric, and normalized reward-margin procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3.2 and 5 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the learning-rate and beta sensitivity analyses and the tests of intermediate representations and reference-distribution effects. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed evaluations and standard-deviation reporting in tables, captions, and error bars. No run-count or uncertainty-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are retained throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports UltraFeedback in-distribution accuracy of 0.752 for EX-RM and 0.646 for IM-RM in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, and Appendix A–B derivations and proofs are unchanged. Theorem 2 merely adds an explicit reference to the already-defined loss in Equation (3).

C1.justification: The central claims remain stronger IM-RM reliance on superficial tokens, weaker generalization under token-level shifts, and verification without learning to generate. The rewritten introduction and conclusion retain these contributions and the existing distinction between token-level and domain shifts.

C2.justification: A new Section 6 paragraph clarifies that generation-verification gaps could explain DPO-versus-RLHF generation performance without explaining the reward-model accuracy gap. It also tentatively extends the token-cue explanation to DPO. Existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same templates, data-processing instructions, GPT-4.1 version and prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and code/data access links. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a focused DPO-versus-RLHF discussion that repositions Swamy et al. (2025), whose citation is removed from the rejected hypothesis in Sections 1 and 3. It also removes the explicit dismissal of the practical implications of Shi et al. (2025).

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits across the abstract, introduction, results, and conclusion, adds a related-work paragraph, and updates bibliographic metadata. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4's caption now identifies the displayed responses as examples. Minor spacing, link-color, and text-reflow changes occur, including the limitations and references. The figures, plots, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Section 6 discussion distinguishes reward-model ranking accuracy from downstream DPO/RLHF performance, reducing ambiguity in v1's treatment of the generation-verification argument and prior work. This improves conceptual precision, while the unchanged theory and experimental evidence keep the overall gain limited.
